newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.
newsitem.headline: Soy shipping conditions at key Brazilian ports.

text.p: The Brazilian ports of Paranagua and Santos reported the following conditions for shipping soybeans and soy products:

Vessels: Avon loading 19,500 tonnes soybeans/meal. Velos loading 51,258 tonnes soymeal. Sotiras loading 52,500 tonnes soybeans. Waiting to dock, 10 vessels to load soymeal, eight to load soybeans and two to load mixed cargo (soybeans/meal). Road: 1,146 trucks carrying soybeans arrived on April 23, 403 trucks with soymeal and 100 with vegetable oils, including soyoil.

Loading: 33,705 tonnes soybeans, 17,279 tonnes soymeal. In the year to April 23, Paranagua loaded 1.53 million tonnes of soybeans, up from 772,203 tonnes in the same period in 1996. Soymeal loadings were 1.44 million, down from 1.72 million in the previous year.

Vessels: Stefania loading 28,400 tonnes soymeal. Waiting to dock, Glory Hope to load 53,000 tonnes soybeans and Horizon to load 55,000 tonnes soybeans. At Cargill private terminal, Orleta Lwowskie loading 57,855 tonnes soybeans. Finix waiting to dock, to load 24,900 tonnes soybeans.

The port loaded 41,500 tonnes soybeans, 148,340 tonnes soymeal and 39,340 tonnes soyoil in the month to April 23. This compared with a total of 16,600 tonnes soybeans, 135,148 tonnes soymeal and 5,000 tonnes soyoil in April 1996.
Latest available figures show that in March, the port loaded 108,119 tonnes soymeal, up 62 percent from 66,943 tonnes the previous year. No soybeans or soyoil were loaded in March of either year.
